issues.location: Kleene matrix languages and no-tautology proposition, source lines 48, 92 and 134–146
issues.finding: Both matrices name the standard propositional language L_0 but supply truth functions only for four nonnullary connectives. The earlier L_0 formation rules can include nullary truth or falsity constants under reader tags. If a falsity constant is interpreted as False, its negation is a tautology in both Kleene systems, contradicting the proposition; the proof that every formula becomes Undef under the all-Undef variable assignment also fails for constants. Other primitive connectives, if present, likewise lack interpretations here.
issues.proposed_resolution: Specify in both target matrices the constant-free fragment generated by variables and the four displayed connectives. Read the proposition and proof within that restricted language, where the all-Undef induction is valid. Preserve the frozen source unchanged.

translation_treatment: The target translates the sequential and parallel computational motivations, both truth-function matrices, the no-tautology proof, consequence exercise, and Bochvar extension. It explicitly restricts both matrices to the constant-free four-connective fragment so that the claimed theorem has its proved scope.
